verdict.rationale: Ironclad documents a broad public API: the Records API creates, retrieves and updates records, the Workflows API launches and interacts with workflows, and the API also covers approvals, document versions, webhooks and data exports. Its own docs also show UI-only steps. Workflows must be published in Workflow Designer before they can be launched via API, OAuth clients are registered through an in-app page, and API access requires an add-on, so full UI parity is not shown. Missing for 10: workflow design and publishing via API, client registration via API, a parity statement or complete API reference (OpenAPI spec paths returned 404), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The corresponding Records API allows you to retrieve, update, and create records.
The corresponding Workflows API allows you to retrieve, create, and interact with active and completed workflows.
Integrations can also directly control the contract process, automatically blocking or pushing forward approvals.
it is possible to create and retrieve webhooks in the UI and through the API
In Workflow Designer, publish the workflow you wish to launch if it has not been published already.
